newsitem.title: GERMANY: Chirac sees EMU on time, urges more savings - paper.
newsitem.headline: Chirac sees EMU on time, urges more savings - paper.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac was quoted on Tuesday as confirming the timetable for Europe's currency union would be maintained and that considerable savings efforts were still necessary.

In an interview published in Tuesday's edition of the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung Chirac said he confirmed an agreement reached with Chancellor Kohl last week that the Maastricht Treaty would be upheld.

The Treaty says that currency union should begin on January 1, 1999 with those nations meeting the strict entry criteria. This includes having a budget deficit of no more than three percent of gross domestic product.
Chirac said that to reach that goal further savings efforts were necessary as both nations had not yet reached the three percent level, the paper said.
All other policies would be a historic mistake, Chirac said, according to the newspaper.
